perspective:
From Christian Mensah’s available perspective:

- He is a police officer and knows Jonathan Balogun as his childhood best friend; he often seeks Jonathan’s advice and values his more educated perspective.
- He felt anxious and suspicious that Jonathan was hiding something important, so he arranged and attended a meeting with Jonathan at their favorite coffee shop.
- He confronted Jonathan, saying he felt Jonathan was hiding something. Jonathan replied that Christian could trust him, then admitted he had been hiding something: he is in some trouble and didn’t know how to tell Christian.
- Christian offered help and support. Jonathan said the situation was complicated and he didn’t want to drag Christian into it, but he could use support and resources to get out of a mess.
- Christian asked whether the trouble was related to anything illegal. Jonathan said he couldn’t say for sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he didn’t do anything illegal himself.
- Christian told Jonathan he would look into the matter discreetly. Jonathan thanked him and said he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.
- Christian’s investigation led him to believe Jonathan is being framed or set up by someone. He told Jonathan this, said he had leads, and planned to gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence.
- Christian later believed/found out that the real culprit is someone both he and Jonathan know and trust. He felt betrayed and resolved to confront that person and bring them to justice. He told Jonathan this; Jonathan warned him the person is dangerous and trusted Christian to do what is right.
- Christian’s own actions/decisions include confronting Jonathan, offering help, asking about illegal involvement, investigating discreetly, gathering evidence, and planning to confront the culprit.
- The exact identity of the culprit is not named in the provided dialogue, but Christian believes he has found out who it is.
